title: SEO and AEO for Contractors | Vestis Solutions
description: SEO and AEO for contractors: show up on Google, Google Maps, ChatGPT and Gemini when locals ask who to call. No ranking guarantees, just steady work.
h1: SEO and AEO for contractors who want the phone to ring
intro: You do good work, but when someone nearby searches for what you do, a competitor shows up first. Your Google profile is half filled out, your website is a few years old, and you have no idea if ChatGPT even knows you exist. SEO and AEO for contractors fixes that, one piece at a time.
definition: SEO (search engine optimization) is the work that helps your business show up in Google search and Google Maps. AEO (answer engine optimization) is the work that helps your business get named when people ask AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini who to hire.

sections.h2: Why SEO and AEO for contractors matter now
paras: Homeowners and property managers still search Google. More of them now also ask ChatGPT or Gemini questions like "who is a good roofer near me" and get a short list of names back. If your business is not in that list, you never get the call.

Both kinds of search reward the same basics: clear information about what you do, where you do it, and proof that real customers trust you. Get those right and you give yourself a fair shot in both places.
Every month, I work on the pieces that tell Google and AI tools who you are and why you are a good pick.
bullets: Google Business Profile: correct categories, service areas, hours, photos and regular posts.
Service pages: one clear page for each service you want more of, written the way customers ask.
Reviews: a simple, repeatable way to ask happy customers for a review, and to reply to every one.
Consistent info across the web: your name, address and phone number matching everywhere they appear.
Plain answers on your site to the questions customers actually ask, so AI tools have something to quote.

paras: No one can guarantee a ranking on Google or a mention in ChatGPT. Anyone who does is guessing or selling something. Google and the AI companies change how they rank results, and they do not ask anyone's permission.
What I can promise is steady, honest work on the things that matter, and a monthly look at what changed: calls, form fills, map views and where you show up.

SEO and AEO run in the background of every partnership, starting in the first two weeks. More leads only help if your team can handle them, so I also look at how leads are answered and followed up. I am based in Charlotte, NC, and work with contractors across the US.
Partnerships start at $3,000 a month for the first 90 days, then month to month. Paid ads are optional and extra.

signs: Competitors with fewer reviews show up above you on Google Maps.
Your Google Business Profile has not been touched in months.
Your website has one page that lists every service.
You asked ChatGPT for a contractor in your area and your name did not come up.
Your phone number or address is different on different sites.

faq.a: AEO is the work that helps your business get named when people ask AI tools like ChatGPT or Gemini who to hire. Those tools pull from websites, reviews and business listings. When your information is clear, consistent and backed by good reviews, you give them a reason to mention you.

They overlap a lot, but the goal is slightly different. SEO aims to rank your pages in Google search and Google Maps. AEO aims to get your business quoted or recommended inside an AI answer. Most of the groundwork, like a complete Google profile, strong service pages and reviews, helps both.

faq.q: How long does SEO take for a contractor?
faq.a: Most contractors see early movement in a few months, not a few weeks. Fixing your Google Business Profile and listings can help sooner. Service pages and reviews build up over time. How fast depends on your market, your competition and where you are starting from.

faq.q: Can you guarantee I will rank first on Google?
faq.a: No, and no one honestly can. Google and AI companies decide rankings, and they change how they do it often. What I commit to is the work itself: a complete profile, strong service pages and a steady way to ask for reviews.

faq.q: How do I get my business to show up in ChatGPT?
faq.a: Make it easy for AI tools to understand and trust your business. That means a clear website with a page for each service and area, a complete Google Business Profile, steady reviews, and the same name, address and phone number everywhere. There is no switch to flip, only consistent work.

faq.q: Do reviews really matter for contractor SEO?
faq.a: Yes, reviews are one of the strongest signals for Google Maps and for AI answers. Both look at how many reviews you have, how recent they are and what customers say. A simple habit of asking after every finished job usually does more than any one-time push.
